proposal.name: Show which Gobra proofs ran out of time

plan.name: Show which Gobra proofs ran out of time
plan.summary: Keep D-0144's 20-minute container backstop and gate-error outcome, and give Gobra a 19-minute-30-second --packageTimeout so it can report before the backstop; this deliberately reduces proof time without increasing the maximum wait, as F1 A decides. Mount a fresh writable report directory beside read-only /work, request -g and the logging needed for the pinned image's unfinished-member messages, read stats.json after success, failure and timeout, and recognize both the exit-1 member timeout and exit-0 package timeout as errors: map reported member IDs to source files and receiver-qualified names with go/ast, count a Go member completed only when all its Viper members have verified=true, sum their millisecond times, and treat success=false as a completed failed proof rather than unfinished. Include every reported unfinished member and every completed member's time in timeout errors reaching the agent's gate tool, final-gate factory post and CI, and include completed members in descending time order in ordinary gate feedback and receipts; missing or unreadable reports explicitly leave selected source members 'not reported', never active or completed, preserve any actual unfinished-member messages, and neither invent timings nor change ordinary verification outcomes or evidence fingerprints. Extend the existing Gobra parser and deadline tests, preserve existing function/contract lists and Docker isolation, and add regression coverage backed by unedited stdout/stderr and stats.json captured from the pinned Gobra image for a finished run and a timeout containing both completed and unfinished members, with their exact Go sources and reproduction commands, plus an integration-tagged real-tool test in internal/verify that proves a deliberately expensive function times out under a short package limit and is named before the container backstop (the quick nonlinear counterexample in the discussion is not that fixture). Update SPEC.md, citing this ratified plan, and docs/gate.md to explain the two limits, the lost proof time, report semantics and fallback, diagnostic-only timings, capture provenance and real-tool test command; extract the existing modeled MCP gate closure as modeledGateTool and use it in mcpCmd so the same staging, verification, error response and gate-run logging are tested offline, and remove each run's report directory after reading it, including on cancellation.

tests.name: TestGobra946CapturedReports
tests.says: The parser consumes pinned-image captures, distinguishes completed and unfinished Viper members, retains completed failures, and maps Go methods to source without confusing receivers.

tests.name: TestGobra946RunCollectsStatistics
tests.says: The actual Docker boundary requests the inner deadline and writable statistics output, consumes it on success, failure and timeout, and cleans it up.

tests.name: TestGobra946BothTimeoutShapes
tests.says: The exact member and package timeout messages supplied in the issue remain gate errors at exit 1 and exit 0, with source-qualified unfinished members and honest missing-report fallback.

tests.name: TestGobra946BackstopNamesOnlySelectedSources
tests.says: A killed run names selected functions and distinct receivers as not reported, excludes explorer and test functions, and fabricates no completed timing.

tests.name: TestGobra946FinishedGateShowsMeasuredTimes
tests.says: Measured member times survive Go verification into feedback and CI receipts, slowest first, but do not alter evidence fingerprints or mutate the report.

tests.name: TestGobra946CIGateNamesUnfinishedProof
tests.says: The real verify command exits as a gate error and logs the unfinished method and its file, excluding the unselected Successors explorer.

tests.name: TestGobra946AgentGateNamesUnfinishedProof
tests.says: The modeled MCP gate returns the same timeout detail as an error and retains it in the build's gate-run log.

tests.name: TestGobra946FactoryPostNamesUnfinishedProof
tests.says: The factory's actual failed-build comment keeps an unfinished member obtained through Gobra, with no active-proof invention and no failed-Code-check receipt.

The first check passed; `repo/` is unchanged, and the resulting change requires a person to merge.

answers.question: D-0144 currently gives the entire Gobra container run a 20-minute deadline. Which limit should #946 use so Gobra's own --packageTimeout can emit unfinished-member diagnostics and stats.json before the container backstop fires?
answers.says: Keep the container backstop at 20 minutes and set Gobra's package timeout to 19 minutes 30 seconds, reserving time within the existing cap for startup and reporting. This preserves the current maximum wait but gives Gobra less proof time; document that tradeoff in the ratified plan, SPEC.md and docs/gate.md.
